page: The Amazon Web Services r8ib.96xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by Intel x86_64 processors running on the AWS Nitro System. This instance features 192 physical cores and 384 dedicated vCPUs operating at a clock speed of up to 3.9 GHz. It provides 3072.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an allocation ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware accelerators are not present, with zero GPUs included.

Storage architecture on the r8ib.96xlarge relies entirely on network-attached options, as the instance contains no local disk volumes. To support heavy input/output operations against external storage services and enable high-speed interconnectivity across distributed systems, the configuration includes a 400 Gbps baseline network bandwidth capability.

By delivering massive memory density alongside extensive core counts and high network throughput, the instance avoids host-level CPU contention for large scale environments. The absence of local disk requires external volume provisioning, making network bandwidth critical to overall throughput. The r8ib.96xlarge is suited for in-memory caching, SAP HANA and enterprise databases, large-scale distributed analytics, high-performance computing, and memory-intensive data processing pipelines.
